podcasts.title: Why the Agent Era Needs a New Operating System | DHH
podcasts.description:
David Heinemeier Hansson thinks the agent era is reopening a window in computing that has been closed for decades: the chance to build a new operating system people actually want to use.

DHH joins a16z General Partners Martin Casado and Anish Acharya to explain why he’s building Omarchy, an agent-first Linux distribution designed around a computer that users can modify simply by asking. They discuss why the command lines, config files, and detailed error messages that once made Linux intimidating now make it unusually well suited to agents, and why DHH believes software development has become cheap enough to challenge decades-old platform lock-in.

But if code is becoming abundant, what still matters? DHH argues that taste, craft, and the willingness to obsess over the final 2% become more important, not less. The conversation moves from tiny teams wielding the productive capacity of thousands of people to open models, competition at the frontier, and the return of hacker, demo, and pseudonymous internet culture.

podcasts.title: How Fast Should We Build Superintelligence? | Nick Bostrom
podcasts.description:
The question isn’t simply whether humanity should race toward superintelligence or stop. Nick Bostrom argues the harder challenge is preserving the ability to slow down when safety falls behind, without turning a temporary pause into permanent technological stagnation.

a16z’s Eddy Lazzarin and Elena Burger sit down with Bostrom to revisit the ideas he helped bring into the mainstream, now that increasingly capable AI systems actually exist. They discuss why alignment may become harder as models grow more situationally aware, which capability improvements may carry more risk than others, and why Bostrom favors “pacing the frontier” rather than committing to a broad or indefinite pause.

They also examine the cost of waiting. Bostrom argues that safely developed superintelligence could radically extend human lifespans and address problems from disease to poverty, meaning delay carries risks of its own. From there, the conversation turns to Deep Utopia, governance, the possibility of post-human forms of life, the simulation argument, and whether AI could eventually surpass humans at philosophy itself.

podcasts.title: Superintelligence Needs the Physical World with CEO and Co-Founder of Arda Bob McGrew
podcasts.description:
Is the AI singularity actually coming? Bob McGrew, former Chief Research Officer at OpenAI, argues that superintelligence won’t arrive without changes in the physical world, and that the “hard takeoff” argument is wrong.

Sarah Guo and Elad Gil sit down with Bob, an early key executive at Palantir who later led research at OpenAI. He is now CEO and co-founder of Arda, which is leveraging AI to make American manufacturing competitive. Bob explains why automating AI researchers is a one-time boost rather than a runaway loop, and why GPUs, compute, wet labs, and factories are the real bottlenecks. 

They cover Arda’s work with Anduril on everything from actuators to missiles to the Fury combat aircraft, why Arda is building “Cursor for manufacturing engineers”, and how the forward deployed engineering model really works. Plus, the big-picture future view: machines that make machines, self-replicating factories, and Bob’s answer to the Fermi paradox.

podcasts.title: Evolution of Digital Assets at Grayscale – Peter Mintzberg (EP.528)
podcasts.description:
Peter Mintzberg is CEO of Grayscale, one of the world's largest digital asset managers founded in 2013.

 
 
Peter joined Grayscale two years ago after a career in strategy and M&A at Goldman Sachs, Apollo, and BlackRock. He saw digital assets as the next step in the evolution of traditional finance.
 
 
Our conversation covers the rapid mainstream adoption of digital assets, Grayscale's transition from its pioneering trusts to a broad ETF platform, and opportunities beyond Bitcoin and Ethereum. We discuss active management in digital assets, the evolution of blockchain applications, and the changing regulatory environment.
 
 
We then turn to Peter's view of what comes next, including the convergence of AI and tokenization, personalized portfolios, and a future where the distinction between liquid and illiquid assets fades away.

podcasts.title: The Missing Layer for Personal AI | First Person Labs’ Ken Liu
podcasts.description:
AI agents are getting smarter, but every new agent still has to learn who you are. What if your preferences, priorities, relationships, and digital context could move with you instead?

First Person Labs co-founder Ken Liu joins a16z’s Martin Casado and Joel de la Garza to introduce Second, a personal context layer designed to understand what you’re doing across your digital life and make that context available to the agents you choose.

They discuss how Second can proactively connect information across conversations and applications, why protecting such personal data requires a different security architecture, and the longer-term vision of AI that doesn’t just respond to prompts, but understands enough context to know when and how to help.
